overview.title: 📖 Overview: Deadlines, Early Shabbat, and a Nasi Deposed
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 27a–27b
overview.hebrewSource: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ ״עַד וְעַד בַּכְּלָל״ — הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הוֹאִיל וּתְנַן בִּבְחִירָתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf opens by settling whether Rabbi Yehuda's 'until' (four hours, seven hours, the midpoint of the afternoon) includes the last hour or not, and proves from tractate Eduyyot that it does. From there it asks whether the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda for the afternoon prayer too, and finds the evidence split: Rav prayed the Shabbat prayer while it was still day, while Rav Huna and his colleagues waited for night. A story of Rav praying early at Geniva's house yields three halakhot and a discussion of what an early Shabbat or early motzaei Shabbat prayer commits one to. The daf closes with the famous confrontation over whether the evening prayer is optional, which ends with Rabban Gamliel removed and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya proposed in his place.

slides.title: ⏳ Does 'Until' Include the Last Hour?
slides.subtitle: The Gemara tests Rabbi Yehuda's 'until seven hours' for Mussaf against a baraita

nodes.content: ❓ Mishna: Mussaf may be recited all day; Rabbi Yehuda says until seven hours. Is 'until' inclusive (עַד וְעַד בַּכְּלָל) or exclusive?
📜 Baraita: if Mussaf and Minḥa are both pending, the Rabbis say Minḥa first (it is frequent, תְּדִירָה); Rabbi Yehuda says Mussaf first, because its time is about to elapse (עוֹבֶרֶת)

columns.label: If exclusive
columns.content: Mussaf would end at the start of the seventh hour (noon), before Minḥa begins half an hour later — the two could never overlap. Rabbi Yehuda's ruling would be impossible.

columns.label: If inclusive
columns.content: Mussaf runs through the seventh hour, so it overlaps with Minḥa. But then what separates Rabbi Yehuda's 'until the midpoint of the afternoon' from the Rabbis' 'until evening'?

nodes.content: 💡 'Midpoint of the afternoon' means the first half of the afternoon period: it ends at eleven hours minus a quarter after sunrise. So Rabbi Yehuda's 'until' is always inclusive.

✅ Rav Naḥman: Eduyyot proves it — Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava testified that the daily morning offering was brought at four hours. Rav Kahana: the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda, since the 'preferred' tractate Eduyyot rules like him.

callout.label: Practical result:
callout.text: The morning prayer may be recited until the end of the fourth hour, and Mussaf until the end of the seventh.

slides.title: 🍞 When Did the Manna Melt? Reading the Hours of the Morning
slides.subtitle: Exodus 16:21 says 'when the sun grew hot it melted' — the Gemara fits that into both views of 'morning'
rows: The Torah's term for full midday heat, when even the shade is hot
'When the sun grew hot it melted' (Exodus 16:21)
Rabbi Aḥa bar Ya'akov: the hour when the sun is hot but the shade is still cool
'Morning by morning' (בַּבֹּקֶר בַּבֹּקֶר) splits it into two mornings, so gathering ended at the end of the third hour
The extra 'morning' moves the end of gathering one hour earlier
The manna's melting at four hours fits both tannaitic clocks; the mishna need not be a third opinion

callout.label: Why this matters:
callout.text: The Gemara first suspected the manna mishna was a 'new position' that fit neither Rabbi Yehuda nor the Rabbis. Reading the doubled 'morning' rescues it for both.

slides.title: 🌇 Minḥa Until Evening or Until the Midpoint? Nobody Rules
slides.subtitle: Rav Ḥisda looks for a decision and finds the practice of the Sages divided

lines.speaker: Rav Ḥisda
lines.text: For the morning prayer Rav Kahana ruled like Rabbi Yehuda because of Eduyyot. Here, for the afternoon prayer, what is the ruling?

lines.speaker: Rav Yitzḥak
lines.text: He was silent and said nothing — he knew of no established ruling.

lines.speaker: Rav Ḥisda
lines.text: Let us see for ourselves: Rav prayed the Shabbat prayer on Shabbat eve while it was still day. Learn from this that the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda, and Minḥa ends at the midpoint of the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: On the contrary! Rav Huna and the Sages would not pray until evening. Learn from that that the halakha does not follow Rabbi Yehuda.

lines.speaker: Conclusion
lines.text: Since the halakha was stated neither like this Master nor like that Master: one who acts like this one has acted legitimately, and one who acts like that one has acted legitimately (דַּעֲבַד כְּמָר עֲבַד).

lines.speaker: Story
lines.text: Rav visited Geniva's house and prayed the Shabbat prayer on Shabbat eve. Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba prayed behind him, and Rav did not step back to interrupt him. Three halakhot: one may pray Shabbat's prayer on Shabbat eve; a student may pray behind his rabbi; it is forbidden to pass before one who is praying.

callout.label: Two objections answered:
callout.text: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi did pass before people praying — but beyond four cubits. And Rabbi Yirmeya prayed behind Rav even though Rav taught never to pray next to or behind one's rabbi (Rabbi Eliezer adds that this drives away the Divine Presence) — because Rabbi Yirmeya was a disciple-colleague (תַּלְמִיד חָבֵר), which is why he could ask Rav directly, 'Did you separate from labor?'

slides.title: 🕯️ Praying Shabbat In and Out Before Its Time
slides.subtitle: What does an early Shabbat or early motzaei Shabbat prayer commit you to?

boxes.title: Early Shabbat prayer (Rav)
items: Rav prayed the Shabbat prayer on Shabbat eve while it was still day
Rav told Rabbi Yirmeya he had separated from labor
Rav Naḥman in Shmuel's name: one may also recite kiddush over the cup before nightfall — and the halakha follows him
Rabbi Yishmael (or, per Ulla, Rabbi Elazar) son of Rabbi Yosei did the same beside a pillar (or a palm tree)

boxes.title: Early motzaei Shabbat prayer (Rabbi Yoshiya)
items: Rabbi Yoshiya would pray the motzaei Shabbat evening prayer while it was still Shabbat
Rav Yehuda in Shmuel's name: one may recite havdala over the cup after that early prayer
Ulla's version of the pillar story is exactly this case: motzaei Shabbat prayed on Shabbat

boxes.title: Prayed early by mistake
items: Rav Dimi bar Liva'ei prayed Shabbat's prayer on a cloudy day thinking it was night; Abaye let him fumigate baskets afterward — an error does not bind him
A community prayed the motzaei Shabbat prayer on Shabbat when clouds darkened the sky; when the sun reappeared Rabbi ruled: since they prayed, they prayed
Why the difference? A community is different — we do not burden them to pray again

callout.label: Side question:
callout.text: Rabbi Avin reported that Rabbi prayed the Shabbat prayer early, then entered the bathhouse and taught afterward. Rava: he entered only to perspire, and this was before the Sages decreed against that on Shabbat.

slides.title: 🌙 'Is the Evening Prayer Optional?' — The Day Rabban Gamliel Was Deposed
slides.subtitle: The mishna's 'evening prayer has no fixed time' follows the view that it is optional (רְשׁוּת)

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rav Yehuda in Shmuel's name: Rabban Gamliel says the evening prayer is obligatory (חוֹבָה); Rabbi Yehoshua says optional. Abaye rules obligatory; Rava rules optional

2️⃣ A student asks Rabbi Yehoshua: optional. He asks Rabban Gamliel: obligatory. 'But Rabbi Yehoshua told me optional!' — 'Wait until the masters of the shields (בַּעֲלֵי תְּרִיסִין) enter the study hall'
3️⃣ In public, Rabban Gamliel asks: does anyone dispute this? Rabbi Yehoshua, in deference to the Nasi, says no. 'Yehoshua, stand on your feet and they will testify against you!'
4️⃣ Rabbi Yehoshua: 'If I were alive and he dead, the living could contradict the dead. Now that both are alive, how can the living contradict the living?'
5️⃣ Rabban Gamliel keeps lecturing while Rabbi Yehoshua stands, until the people tell Ḥutzpit the disseminator: 'Stop!' — and he stops
6️⃣ 'How long will he afflict him? Rosh HaShana last year, the firstborn case of Rabbi Tzadok, now this. Let us remove him!'
7️⃣ Not Rabbi Yehoshua (party to the incident), not Rabbi Akiva (no ancestral merit to protect him). Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya: wise, rich, tenth generation from Ezra. He goes to consult his wife

callout.label: Why each qualification:
callout.text: Wise — he can answer Rabban Gamliel's challenges. Rich — he can afford to represent Israel at Caesar's court. Descendant of Ezra — ancestral merit shields him from being punished through Rabban Gamliel's resentment.

summary.principle: Rabbi Yehuda's 'until' is inclusive and the halakha follows him for the morning prayer, but for the afternoon prayer no ruling was issued — and the same daf that permits praying Shabbat early tells how a dispute over the evening prayer cost Rabban Gamliel his office.

flowSteps.content: ❓ Is 'until seven hours' inclusive? The baraita on Mussaf vs. Minḥa only works if it is
📜 Eduyyot: morning offering brought at four hours → 'until and including'; Rav Kahana: halakha like Rabbi Yehuda for Shaḥarit

columns.content: 🌇 Minḥa: Rav prayed early, Rav Huna waited → no ruling; either way is legitimate
🕯️ Early Shabbat prayer + kiddush; early motzaei Shabbat prayer + havdala (Shmuel)

flowSteps.content: 🌙 Evening prayer: Rabban Gamliel obligatory, Rabbi Yehoshua optional; public humiliation → Rabban Gamliel deposed, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya proposed
🎓 Key Principle: where the Sages left a dispute undecided, whoever follows either view has acted properly (דַּעֲבַד כְּמָר עֲבַד)

quiz.q: How does the Gemara finally prove that Rabbi Yehuda's 'until' means 'until and including'?
o: From the verse 'in the heat of the day'
From Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava's testimony in Eduyyot that the morning offering was brought at four hours
From the fact that Minḥa is more frequent than Mussaf
From Rav praying the Shabbat prayer early
quiz.e: Rav Naḥman cites the Eduyyot mishna: since the daily morning offering was still brought at four hours, Rabbi Yehuda's 'until four hours' must include the fourth hour. Rav Kahana adds that the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda because Eduyyot rules like him.

quiz.q: What does the Gemara conclude about the deadline for the afternoon prayer?
o: The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda, because Rav prayed the Shabbat prayer early
The halakha follows the Rabbis, because Rav Huna prayed until evening
No ruling was issued, so one who follows either opinion has acted legitimately
One must always wait until evening on Shabbat eve
quiz.e: Rav's early prayer and Rav Huna's late prayer point in opposite directions, so the Gemara concludes that with no ruling stated, whoever acts like either Sage has acted legitimately.

quiz.q: Which halakha is NOT one of the three derived from Rav praying at Geniva's house?
o: One may pray the Shabbat prayer on Shabbat eve before nightfall
A student may pray behind his rabbi
It is forbidden to pass before those who are praying
Kiddush may be recited only after the stars emerge
quiz.e: The three derivations are: praying Shabbat's prayer early, a student praying behind his rabbi, and not passing before one who is praying. Kiddush before nightfall is in fact permitted, per Rav Naḥman in Shmuel's name.

quiz.q: A community mistakenly recited the motzaei Shabbat prayer on Shabbat because clouds made it look like night. What did Rabbi rule?
o: They must pray again, because a mistaken prayer is void
Since they prayed, they prayed — a community is not burdened to repeat
They must recite havdala immediately
They may perform labor since Shabbat had ended for them
quiz.e: Rabbi ruled that their prayer stands. The Gemara explains that this leniency is because a community is different: we do not burden them to pray again, unlike Rav Dimi's individual mistake.

quiz.q: Why did the Sages choose Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya to replace Rabban Gamliel rather than Rabbi Akiva?
o: Rabbi Akiva was too old
Rabbi Akiva was party to the incident with Rabban Gamliel
Rabbi Akiva lacked ancestral merit and might be punished through Rabban Gamliel's resentment
Rabbi Akiva had already refused the position
quiz.e: Rabbi Yehoshua was rejected because he was party to the incident; Rabbi Akiva because, descending from converts, he lacked the merit of ancestors to protect him. Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya was wise, rich, and a tenth-generation descendant of Ezra.
